items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: One of them I did for Gerry and it was not his style either; he didn't want to do it.

ctx.x: soft and some of the most exciting things were very very soft, like a whisper sometimes, to come down from something loud into that.

It struck me when I heard the things that you did for Red, you're familiar with Gerry Mulligan's concert bands of the early sitties, and it struck me how much the charts that Mulligan and Bob Brookmeyer and Gary McFarland did twenty five years later, how much they sounded like what you had done in the late thirties.

It is the same very light, very woodwindish sort of colorations, a lot of clarinet lead in the reed section, but using the clarinet and the lower and middle registers. There's a lot of similarity, I was surprised by that.
